title: The Results Are In: Voters Hate Data Centers
gist: The 2026 US midterms were a broad rebuke of the data center buildout: anti-data-center Democrats won Senate, House and governor races (including moratorium backers in Georgia and Texas), nine states' ballot measures rejected construction or approved moratoriums, and industry super PAC money failed to save its candidates. Strategists expect the end of favorable tax breaks, tougher regulators and stricter environmental enforcement, threatening hundreds of planned projects.

themes.theme: Data centers as a decisive midterm issue

insights.claim: In 2026 midterm exit polling by NBC News, almost a quarter of voters said data centers were crucial to their vote and nearly two-thirds said they were a major or minor factor.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Data center opposition is now a mass electoral issue, raising political risk for AI infrastructure capex.

themes.theme: Moratorium risk in Texas and Georgia hubs

insights.claim: Democrats Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia and Gina Hinojosa in Texas won governor races in upsets while campaigning for data center moratoriums, and Cindy Holscher was near a potential win in Kansas on a similar platform.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Governors with moratorium mandates in the two largest development hubs directly threaten hyperscaler build pipelines.

insights.claim: A data center pause in Texas and Georgia, two of the biggest US development hubs, could have serious implications for the hundreds of projects planned in each state.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott

insights.so_what: Local ballot mechanisms give communities a direct veto that can strand sites and land deals.

themes.theme: Industry money failing at the polls

insights.claim: Industry super PAC Building the Future spent $1.5 million backing Darline Graham in South Carolina, who lost to moratorium supporter Annie Andrews, and more than $1.5 million backing Ty Masterson in the Kansas governor race.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: AI/data center political spending showed weak returns, so industry lobbying power may be overestimated.

insights.claim: Michigan Democrat Will Lawrence, who centered his campaign on AI and data center regulation, declared victory over Republican Tom Barrett, who received $340,000 from Elon Musk's America PAC.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Musk-linked political money did not overcome anti-AI sentiment in a high-spend race.
